s.g: A coxswain of a boat, especially of a racing crew.
(ambitransitive) To act as coxswain for.
s.x: The physicist Stephen Hawking used to cox for a college rowing team.

s.g: (anatomy) The basal segment of a limb of various arthropods (insects and spiders, for example).
(anatomy) sciatic (relating to the hip)
(zoology) Relating to a coxite
(historical) The cap of a court jester, adorned with a red stripe.
The fleshy red pate of a rooster.
(by extension) A foolish or conceited person; a dandy.

coxed.f: simple past and past participle of cox

s.g: Having a cox
(Canada, slang) A coxswain.

coxing.f: present participle and gerund of cox

s.g: (rowing) Not having a cox.
Any of several viruses of the genus Enterovirus similar to poliovirus
Any of many enteroviruses that cause disease mostly in children.
In a ship's boat, the helmsman given charge of the boat's crew.
(rowing) The member of a crew who steers the shell and coordinates the power and rhythm of the rowers.
(naval) A rank or position.
(archaic) The second or third mate of a vessel, in charge of the master's barge.
(transitive, intransitive) To act as coxswain for.
(obsolete) Cocky.
(veterinary medicine, informal) Coccidiosis.
